Previous revision 829b089bf6636af9ffed1f333b103e4e383f7b48 (10 Oct 2026), served from the un-keyed weights_3bit.previous_default_dir
common.note: All modes use the W8A16 drafter view (mtp/mtp-draft-e4m3.safetensors, shipped in the checkpoint repo). Default modes decode / prefill-long run W8A8 prompt rows on the native GDN prefill path; the -nopf modes drop the two native-prefill flags (exact-arithmetic prefill, about 7 % slower). Numbers in README.md / BENCHMARKS.md were measured on the shipped image through launch-flashnext.py.

prefix_caching.note: opt-in (launcher --prefix-caching): align-mode prefix caching on the recurrent state; the attention block is set explicitly to 2048 (--block-size 2048) = the mamba block, so a prefix hit resumes on a block boundary and is bit-identical to a cold start (without it vLLM picks 1696 and hits differ from cold; checked 12 Oct 2026); served gates 10 Oct 2026: 64K repeat 9.6 s -> 0.35 s TTFT with identical output; needles 131K + 200K 40/40

host_pools.note: HSA_USERPTR_FOR_PAGED_MEM=0: ROCm allocates the host tables as GTT buffers instead of registered user pointers, so host memory compaction no longer invalidates them (KFD eviction stalls under load 2.7 s -> 0.07 s over a 3-minute run at 8 requests, speed unchanged). They count against the first GPU's GTT size: 56,116 MiB above the idle baseline at ready (decode mode, 10 Oct).
host_pools.note_3bit: 3-bit modes default to ROCm user-pointer pools (the published 10 Oct behaviour and VRAM peaks); --host-pools gtt is their opt-in: it removes the occasional memory pauses under load and costs ~1 GiB VRAM in decode (rel3s vs rel3u, 12 Oct)

ple_host.note: launcher --ple-host pageable (or auto on hosts whose GTT limit cannot hold the pinned tables), 4-bit modes 4bit, 4bit-cache and 4bit-long: the per-layer embedding (PLE) tables (24.44 GiB per rank, E4M3) stay in ordinary pageable host memory (anonymous mmap, transparent huge pages, mlocked when RLIMIT_MEMLOCK allows) instead of pinned GTT memory; the GPU's gathers go through a host worker pool. Pinned host memory 95.5 -> 46.6 GiB (GTT at ready, 13 Oct), so the GTT pools fit the default GTT limit (half the RAM) of a 128 GB host; the RAM need is unchanged. Gate 13 Oct under a 118 GiB container memory limit: 4bit C1 176.2 / C8 403.4 (pinned 177.2 / 400.7), 4bit-cache 159.0 / 323.3 (pinned 157.0 / 324.7), output bit-identical. Needs an image with the pageable PLE runtime (images); the published 4-bit image keeps the tables pinned.

filebacked.note: opt-in (launcher --ple-host filebacked; auto on modes marked ple_filebacked when MemAvailable cannot keep the PLE tables resident): the E4M3 PLE export laid out once as two raw files next to the weights (<weights>-ple-raw: codes.e4m3 + row_scale.f32, ~50 GB) and mmapped read-only by each rank, so the tables live in the page cache (shared, evictable, read from disk on a miss) instead of resident process memory; the same host gather as pageable, so the output is the same. Needs an image with the file-backed runtime (images).

common.resident_gib_note: resident_gib: host RAM a running server keeps per PLE layout (pinned / GTT + pageable + its processes), measured 14 Oct at ready and under load (memory-cgroup + GTT accounting): 4bit pinned 108.5, pageable ~110, file-backed with user-pointer pools 60.9; 4bit-long 108.4 / 109.9 / 60.9; 4bit-cache file-backed 60.9 (user-pointer pools: no RAM prefix tier). 4bit-cache pinned / pageable = 4bit + its 8 GiB RAM prefix tier (derived). The launcher picks the first layout whose value + 6 GiB fits MemAvailable.

expert_cold.note: launcher --expert-cold (auto on hosts where even the file-backed layout does not fit MemAvailable): the coldest share of each decoder layer's experts (by the routing counts) leaves the pinned host pool for one file per GPU (<weights>-expert-cold, written at the first start, reused after); before each MoE launch a gate kernel reads the routed ones into a pinned bounce buffer. Same output, slower. Needs an image with the cold-expert runtime (images). Measured 15 Oct on the r4 image under a 60 GiB memory limit (a 64 GB host), with the reuse cache (384 slots per GPU) and the file-backed PLE layout: cold share 0.2 keeps about 51 GiB of host RAM in use while serving (the memory limit fills with page cache from the file-backed files, as designed), output identical to the pinned layout; --mode 4bit about 85 tok/s single-stream and 181 at 8 requests, --mode 4bit-long about 89 / 237 with needles at 131K tokens 5/5. Share 0.1 (about 55 GiB, measured 14 Oct without the reuse cache) is picked only where it fits (about 72 GB and up).
